narrative:
The model determined that you have a 36% chance of being a bad credit risk. While this is not an overwhelming majority, it was high enough for the bank to deny your loan application.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this decision were the status of your checking account, how long you have lived at your current residence, and the length of the loan you requested. Your checking account status was the single biggest reason for the denial. Having between 0 and 200 DM in your account is relatively uncommon among approved applicants and pushed the prediction noticeably toward bad credit risk. In contrast, the fact that you have lived in your current home for only one year worked in your favor; shorter time at the same address actually pulled the prediction toward approval. Similarly, requesting a 12-month loan—well below the average of 19 months among those who were approved—also helped your case by reducing the risk score.

Even though two of the top three factors leaned in a positive direction, the negative impact from your checking account status was strong enough to outweigh them and tip the overall prediction above the bank's acceptance threshold.

You should focus on building a healthier balance in your checking account over the next few months, then reapply. This single change is likely to have the largest positive effect on future decisions.
